sadārum: to set in a row, put in order; of an account, to write out, list: isaddar(ma) “he shall write out”. Harper files the same forms under šaṭāru “to write”; the reading sadārum rests on the plate sign SA (not ŠA) in i-sa-ad-dar-ma
manûm-count: to count, reckon (the verb; the noun manûm “mina” is another word): imannû(ma) “they shall count” — 3rd plural, impersonal
tadmiqtum: a favour, a kindness (from damāqum “to be good”; Harper tadmiqtu “favor”): ana tadmiqtim “as a favour”; the commercial sense, an advance made on trust, is a guess from the context
nadûm-Š: Š-stem of nadûm “to throw”: to make (someone) throw down, to strip of: uštaddišu (perfect, with -šu) “he made him throw (it) down”
šipātum: wool (written SIG, as Harper’s glossary gives it): šipâtam (accusative; Harper šipâtu)
šamnum: oil, fat (written Ì.GIŠ, the signs NI + GIŠ): šamnam (accusative; Harper šamnu)
kanīkum: sealed receipt, sealed tablet (from kanākum “to seal”): kanīk kaspim “a sealed receipt for silver”, kanīkim (genitive); not the same word as kunukkum “seal”
egûm: to be careless, neglect (Harper: “to be careless”): itēgi(ma) “he has been negligent, and”
nikkazzum: UNCERTAIN: account, credit (Harper nikkazzu; modern editions normalise nikkassum “account, reckoning”): ana nikkazzim “to the account”, spelled ni-ik-ka-az-zi-im; the sense “account” or “credit” is not secure
qiāpum: to entrust, give in trust (Harper “to intrust”, listed under qâpu): iqīp(ma) “he entrusted (the agent), and”
šikarum: beer (written KAŠ; Harper šikaru): šikarim (genitive), also as the price or rate “of beer”
abnum: stone; a stone used as a weight (written NA₄; Harper abnu): ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone”
sābītum: UNCERTAIN: the tavern-keeper, the woman who brews and sells beer (written ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA, “woman” + “wine”); the reading sābītum follows the modern editors — Harper gives only the signs
ṣarrūtum: criminals, rogues, rebels (Harper: “outlaws, rowdies, traitors”): ṣarrūtum, ṣarrūtim (plural noun, not a title)
rakāsum-N: N-stem of rakāsum “to bind”: to gather, band together, conspire (Harper “collect”): ittarkasū(ma) “they have gathered, and”
šunūti: them (masculine plural, accusative): ṣarrūtim šunūti “those criminals”
šī: she, that (feminine pronoun, as the independent word): ŠAL.GEŠ.TIN.NA šī “that tavern-keeper”; the masculine is šū
redûm-lead: to lead, drive, bring (the verb; rēdûm “soldier” is another word; Harper “to conduct”): irdiam “she led (them) here”, with the ventive -am
gagûm: UNCERTAIN: the cloister, the walled house in which the priestesses of the law lived (written MAL.GE.A, with the sign GE as GI₄ on the plate; Harper leaves the signs unread): ina gagîm “in the cloister”
karānum: wine (written GEŠ.TIN.NA; Harper karânu): bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (É + GEŠ.TIN.NA)
erēbum: to enter: iterub “she has entered” (perfect; Harper I,2)
awīltum: woman, lady (feminine of awīlum; Harper awiltu): awīltam “woman” (accusative)
qalûm: to burn (Harper qalû): iqallû(ši) “they shall burn (her)”
dibtum: UNCERTAIN: credit, a loan on trust — Harper’s diptu “credit(?)”, with his own question mark: ana dibtim “on credit”
usakani: UNCERTAIN: a kind of beer, written U.SA.KA.NI (four signs Harper leaves unread; no meaning known): šikarim usakani “beer of the usakani (kind?)”
3-šu: threefold — the numeral 3 with -šu: adu 3-šu (a-du 3-šu) “three times over” (spoken form reconstructed)
6-šu: sixfold — the numeral 6 with -šu: adu 6-šu (a-du 6-šu) “six times over” (spoken form reconstructed)
-ši: her / it (3rd-person feminine singular suffix, on a verb): ukannūšima “they shall convict her”, inaddûši “they shall throw her”, iqallûši “they shall burn her”
5 BAN₂: fifty qa — the numeral 50 fused with the measure sign (five ban₂ of ten qa each; Harper “L QA”), one ligature on the stone; said ḫamšā qû (spoken form reconstructed). The qa is a measure of capacity

__broaden__.60: sixty — a single vertical wedge (the sexagesimal “one” of the next order); said šūši (?) “sixty” · here before KAŠ “beer”, with the measure (qa) understood and not written: šūši šikarim “sixty (qa) of beer”; spoken form reconstructed
__broaden__.adi: up to, times: adi 12-šu “twelvefold” · as a conjunction, “as long as”, with the subjunctive: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” · adu 3-šu, adu 6-šu “three times, six times (as much)” — the multiplier, spelled a-du (Harper’s variant of adi; the plate has the sign DU)
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going”
__broaden__.amārum: to see, examine: immarūma “they shall examine” · ītamar “he has seen” (perfect, singular) · ītamar (i-ta-mar, perfect) “he saw”: lā ītamar “he did not see”; of a loss, “he met with”: bitiqtam ītamar “he met a loss”
__broaden__.ašrum: place; ana ašrišu “to its (proper) place” · ašar “where”, with a verb in the subjunctive: ašar illiku “where he went”
__broaden__.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša)
__broaden__.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver”
__broaden__.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”
__broaden__.maḫārum: to receive: imḫur(u) · imḫur, imḫuru “he received” (preterite; subjunctive in a clause), imaḫḫar “he shall receive” (present); …ḫari… in a broken form · to face, withstand (litany): qabal lā maḫārim “combat none can face” · imtaḫar (im-ta-ḫar) “she received” (perfect; Harper’s maḫāru I,2, “to receive”): grain and silver for beer
__broaden__.maḫīrum: market rate, price: ana maḫīrātišunu “at their rates” · maḫīr šikarim “the rate of beer” (maḫīr, construct form, written KI.LAM; Harper maḫiru)
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u)
__broaden__.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water”
__broaden__.nakārum: UNCERTAIN: perhaps nakārum “to be hostile, to deny, to dispute”: only the first sign ik survives, which the editor doubts, so the form (ikkir-ma ?) and the sense are a guess; the verb is the editors’ restoration · ittakir (it-ta-ki-ir, perfect) “he denied, disowned (his merchant)”, ittakiršu “he denied him”, ikkiru (ik-ki-ru, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(because) he denied”: here the forms are spelled out on the stele, so the verb nakārum is sure; Harper’s heading is “to be different, to be hostile, to dispute”
__broaden__.našûm: to bear, carry: ittanašši “he shall bear (the penalty)” · našû (na-šu-u, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) he carried”: mimma ša našû “anything that he carried”
__broaden__.pašārum: UNCERTAIN: the verb pašārum “to loosen, release”; in the merchant’s law, perhaps “to sell off, dispose of” (ana pašārim, restored by the editors as “for selling”): only pa-ša… survives, so the form and sense are a guess · ana pašārim (a-na pa-ša-ri-im) “for trading” — Harper’s glossary pašāru I,1 “to trade”: the stele spells the word out, so the form is sure; the sense is Harper’s reading (the editors’ restored “for selling” above was a guess)
__broaden__.qaqqadum: head; the capital, the principal of a loan, as against its interest (written SAG.DU, “head”): ana qaqqadim “to the capital” (genitive, written with the logogram) · qaqqad kaspim “the capital of the silver” (construct form, here spelled ga-ga-ad)
__broaden__.rabûm: great; D/Š-stems “make great”; rabûtim “great (pl.)” · rabîtim (ra-bi-tim, feminine genitive) “large”: ina abnim rabîtim “by the large stone”
__broaden__.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)”
__broaden__.šamallûm: UNCERTAIN: the merchant’s agent, his trading assistant: šamallim (genitive, ša-ma-al-li-im), šamallû (nominative, ša-ma-al-lu-u₂); the editors print a logogram with a complement, so the syllabic spellings are a placeholder · on the stele the word is the Sumerogram ŠÀ.GAN₂.LÁ (Harper SA.GAN.LAL; modern ŠAMAN₂.LÁ), the first two signs one fused group on the plate, so the meaning “agent” is sure and the syllabic spellings above were a placeholder; the case is read from the sentence (šamallûm, šamallâm, šamallîm), also with -šu: šamallīšu “his agent”
__broaden__.šanûm-Š: UNCERTAIN: šanûm “to repeat, do a second time”, so perhaps “to double”; uštašannâ (uš-ta-ša-an-na-ma, with -ma “and”) is a Š-stem perfect (ušta- is the perfect prefix) and is read as “he shall double (it)”, but the exact stem and the form are not secure; the sense follows the penalty of the law · on the stele (§101): uštašannâma (uš-ta-ša-na-ma, with -ma “and”) “he shall double (it)”, which Harper’s glossary lists as a Š-stem perfect of šanû “to duplicate, to double”; the form is as Harper has it and the exact stem is not secure
__broaden__.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · uttēr (ut-te-ir, perfect) “he has given back”: the same verb as utâr
__broaden__.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …” · ūmīšu (UD-mi-šu) “his days”: ūmīšu imannûma “they shall count his days”
__broaden__.ṣabātum: to seize: iṣṣabat, ṣabtu · stative with the subjunctive -u: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” (with Harper’s kirûm: “as long as the orchard is held”) · iṣṣabtamma (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tam-ma) “she seized (them), and” (perfect with the ventive -am and -ma): lā iṣṣabtamma “and she did not seize”
__broaden__.ṣibtum: interest (“increase”): ṣibtam; ṣibassu, ṣibtišu “its interest” · also written MÁŠ (the logogram, “increase”) and ṣib-tam; plural ṣibātim (ṣi-ba-tim) “interest(s)”; ṣibtim genitive · ṣibāt kaspim “the interest on the silver” (ṣibāt, construct form of the plural)
__broaden__.tamkārum: merchant (written tam-KAR §32, DAM.GÀR §40): the ransom-fronting, land-buying businessman of the code · written dam-qar, dam-qar-um (the common syllabic spelling of the merchant): damqar, damqarum “the merchant” (nominative), damqaršu “his merchant” · written DAM.GÀR as a Sumerogram (Harper tamkaru [DAM-GAR]; two signs on the plate): tamkārum, tamkāram, tamkārim, tamkāršu
__broaden__.wašābum: to sit: ul uššab “he shall not sit” (the stone writes uš-ta-ab — a carver’s slip Harper flags) · to dwell: wāšbum (participle, contracted) “the dweller, the tenant” (a conjectured reading, aš-bu-u[m]); wa… “dwell-” in broken forms · stative wašbat (wa-aš-ba-at) “she dwells, lives”: ša ina gagîm lā wašbat “who does not live in the cloister”
__broaden__.wašārum: D-stem (w)uššurum “to release, set free”: ūtaššar “he shall be released” · the form ūtaššar (ū-ta-aš-šar) is the Dt, the t-form of the D-stem, in the present: “he shall be released”; the “D-stem” named above is the stem family, and this form is its t-form (Dt)

ugbabtum: UNCERTAIN: a priestess, written ŠAL.NIN.AN (Harper aššatum NIN.AN; NIN.AN is later written NIN.DINGIR, “lady of the god”); Harper gives no reading and translates only “a priestess”, later editions read ugbabtum, and the ŠAL may be only the woman-sign. The reading rests on the sign group and the context, not on a spelled word
